title: The Eleven O'Clock Ferry
focus: Present perfect passive; reasons and advice

lines.text: Attention all passengers. This is an announcement from Island Ferries.
Due to strong winds, the eleven o'clock ferry to Seal Island has been delayed.
It is now expected to leave at twelve thirty, so we advise passengers to wait in the terminal building.
Tickets for the delayed ferry will remain valid, and no extra payment is required.
If you would prefer to travel tomorrow, you can change your ticket at the information desk.
Passengers with cars should not drive onto the ramp until they are called by the staff.
The café on the first floor is offering a free hot drink to all passengers who are waiting.
Staff will also be handing out blankets to elderly passengers and families with small children.
Please note that the later ferry, which leaves at three, is already full.
We will make another announcement as soon as we have more news. Thank you for your patience.

title: Sixteen and Running a Business

lines.text: My next guest is Leah, who is only sixteen but already runs her own online business. Leah, what do you sell?
I make bracelets from recycled materials, like old fabric and plastic bottle tops.
How did you get the idea?
Last summer, I was helping my aunt clean her garage, and we found boxes full of old clothes. I thought it was a waste to throw them away.
And how did you start selling?
First, I gave bracelets to my friends. They liked them, so I opened a small online shop. In the first month, I sold twelve bracelets.
How many have you sold so far?
More than four hundred. I couldn't believe it when I reached that number.
Do you have time for school as well?
It's difficult. I work on the business at weekends, and I do my homework in the evenings. Sometimes I have to say no to my friends.
What are your plans?
I'd like to hire a friend to help me, and I've been thinking about selling in other countries.
Great ambition. Thank you, Leah.

lines.text: Welcome to Page Turners. This week, I'm talking to Marcus Reed, whose first novel, The Last Lighthouse, has just come out.
Thanks for having me, Sue.
Marcus, the book is set on a small island. Is it a real place?
No, I invented it, but it's inspired by a village where I spent my summers as a child.
How long did it take you to write it?
About four years. I wrote it mostly in the early morning before going to work, because it was the only quiet time I had.
Did you ever want to give up?
Many times. At one point, I'd written two hundred pages and then deleted them all, because I wasn't happy with the story.
That must have been painful!
It was, but the second version was much better. A friend who had read the first draft told me to keep going.
What would you say to people who want to write a book?
Write a little every day, even if it's only ten minutes. And find somebody honest who will read your work.
Wise words. The Last Lighthouse is in bookshops now.

title: Planning the Charity Run

lines.text: Callum, we need to finalise the plans for the charity run. It's in three weeks.
I know. First of all, the route. Should we use the same one as last year?
I think we should change it. The old route goes along a busy road, and it can be dangerous. Why don't we run around the lake instead?
That's a good idea. It's flat and safe, and there's lots of space for the finish line.
Next, the money. Last year we collected about two thousand pounds. This time we'd like to collect more, maybe three thousand.
We could ask local shops to give prizes, and we might offer shirts to everyone who raises more than fifty pounds.
Brilliant. Who is going to design the shirts?
My cousin Alice is studying graphic design. I'll ask her this evening.
And what about helpers? We'll need at least twenty volunteers.
I'm sure we can find them. The students at the sports club have already offered to help.
Wonderful. Let's meet again next Tuesday and check everything.
Agreed. I'll send an email to everybody tonight.

title: Opening a Bank Account

lines.text: Good morning. How can I help you today?
Hello. I'd like to open a bank account, please. I've just started a new job here.
Congratulations. Have you brought some identification and proof of address?
I've brought my passport and a letter from my employer. Is that enough?
The passport is fine, but we also need proof of where you live, like a utility bill or a rental contract.
I have my rental contract on my phone. Can I show you that?
Of course, that's acceptable. Now, would you like a standard account or a student account?
I'm not a student, so the standard one, please.
Okay. You'll receive your card within five working days, and you can set up online banking straight away.
Is there a monthly fee?
There's no fee for the first year. After that, it's three pounds a month, unless you deposit at least a thousand pounds.
That sounds reasonable. What should I do if I lose my card?
Call the number on the back immediately, and we'll block it for you.

title: Two Hosts, Two Opinions

lines.text: Welcome to Screen Time. This week we're reviewing The Silent Sea, a science fiction film about a team of scientists on a space station.
I saw it on Saturday, and honestly, I loved it. The story is slow at the start, but the ending is unforgettable.
I disagree a little. I found the first hour too slow. I almost fell asleep.
Really? I thought the slow beginning made the story more realistic.
Maybe. But I agree about the acting. The lead actress was brilliant. You really believed she was afraid.
And the music was fantastic. It made the scenes much more exciting than the script alone.
What about the special effects?
Better than most films I've seen this year. The space station looked absolutely real.
Would you recommend it to families?
Not to young children. A few scenes are quite scary. But for teenagers and adults, definitely.
I'd give it four stars out of five.
I'd give it four and a half. See you next week, everyone!

title: Planning a Weekend in Lisbon

Great. What time does our flight land on Friday?

What would you like to do first?
I'd like to explore the old streets on foot. People say the city is full of steep hills, so we'd better bring comfortable shoes.
Good idea. And I've read that the food is wonderful. I'd love to try the fresh fish.
Me too. I've made a list of three restaurants, and I'll book one for Saturday night.
What about Sunday?
We could take a train to a small town by the sea. It takes about forty minutes.
Sounds perfect, as long as the weather is nice. If it rains, we'll visit a museum instead.
Deal. Our flight home leaves at six on Sunday evening, so we mustn't be late.

title: The Garden Committee Meets

lines.text: Good evening, everybody. Thanks for coming to the community garden meeting. We have three things to discuss tonight.
First, the water. At the moment, we're paying a lot for water in summer. Does anyone have a suggestion?
We could collect rainwater from the shed roof. My neighbour did that, and it saved him a lot of money.
That's a good idea, Paco, but we'd need to buy a big barrel. How much does one cost?
About forty pounds, I think. We could ask the council to pay for it.
Let's try that. Second, the new members. We've had twelve people ask to join, but we only have six free plots.
Why don't we start a waiting list? And maybe we could share some plots between two families.
I like that. Sharing would also be more social.
Good. Finally, the party. Should we celebrate the end of summer with a barbecue?
Yes! I'll bring salad from my plot, and I can make a big carrot cake.
I'll organise the music, if nobody minds.
Excellent. Let's vote. Who agrees with all three suggestions?
